output:
Short answer — pick an LED task/adjustable desk lamp with high efficacy, good color rendering, adjustable color temperature and dimming, and an ENERGY STAR or DLC certification. From the catalog I found three relevant entries: “Meadowlight Lamp”, “adjustable desk lamps” (category), and “task lamps” (category). The catalog entries lack detailed specs in memory, so you’ll need to verify product-specific claims before purchase.

Why that type of lamp
- LEDs are far more efficient than incandescent/halogen (typical LED fixtures: ~80–150 lm/W vs ~10–20 lm/W for incandescents). This reduces electricity use and heat output.
- Dimming and variable color temperature let you lower power and tailor light for tasks → less overall energy and better comfort.
- Task/adjustable lamps let you light the work surface directly, reducing the need for bright overhead lighting.

Evidence I used
- Catalog search results (memory): found “Meadowlight Lamp”, “adjustable desk lamps”, “task lamps”, and other lighting product categories. (Note: the Meadowlight Lamp entity in memory has no provenance or spec details available.)
- General LED lamp performance and best-practice recommendations described above are standard industry guidance (but specific numbers for a catalog product are not present in the memory results).

What to verify for any candidate lamp (claims you should require evidence for)
- Rated lumen output and wattage (to compute efficacy in lm/W)
- ENERGY STAR or DesignLights Consortium (DLC) certification (if claimed)
- Dimmability and compatibility with your dimmer type (triac, 0–10V, etc.)
- Color temperature range (CCT) and color rendering index (CRI). For office work, CRI ≥ 80 (preferably ≥ 90) and 3500–4000 K often work best.
- Rated lifetime (hours) and LED degradation information (L70 at X hours)
- Flicker specs (important for comfort/productivity)
- Warranty and return policy
- Actual on-desk illuminance (lux) or beam control/glare characteristics
- Price, stock, and lead times

Quick practical checklist (how to choose)
- Look for integrated LED task/adjustable lamp with:
  - Efficacy ≥ 80 lm/W (higher is better)
  - 400–1,000 lumens depending on desk area and target lux (see calculation below)
  - CCT 3000–4000 K for offices, CRI ≥ 80–90
  - Dimming and tilt/arm adjustability
  - ENERGY STAR/DLC certification if possible
- Consider motion sensor/timer or smart controls if the space has intermittent use.

Quick lux → lumens example
- Typical recommended task illuminance: 300–500 lux.
- Desk area example: 1.2 m × 0.6 m = 0.72 m². Required lumens ≈ lux × area.
  - For 500 lux → 500 × 0.72 ≈ 360 lumens on the task surface (account for losses and beam focusing, so choose a lamp rated for 500–800 lumens).
- If you want help with a specific desk size, tell me dimensions and target lux and I’ll compute the needed lumens.

Catalog notes and next steps
- Meadowlight Lamp appears in the catalog results but memory has no provenance/specs saved — verify all specs listed above directly with the product page or vendor.
- If you want, I can:
  - Pull detailed specs for the Meadowlight Lamp if you provide a product page or allow me to search external sources; or
  - Produce a short shortlist of lamp features and sample models (if you tell me geography/price range/style preferences); or
  - Calculate required lumens for your desk if you give dimensions and desired brightness.

Which of those would you like to do next?
